At f7b78e29d the VTA's DIDComm and TSP ingress verifies the received JSON (verify_trust_task_proof_value). The typed re-serializing form is kept only for documents the VTA built itself. The proof's created is kept as a string. So .000Z, +00:00 or fractions verify, wireTimestamp is no longer required for this VTA (it is harmless), and Keyring's comment saying vta-sdk verifies a re-serialization is stale for the pin.
findings.evidence: tt/SPEC.md:310 and pin SPEC.md:309 "MUST verify a proof over the document as received"; vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs:1288-1320 bind_document_to_sender, :1313 verify_trust_task_proof_value(&received, …); vta-sdk/src/trust_task_proof/verify.rs:170-185 "Only for a document this process built (VTI-45)"; affinidi-data-integrity-0.8.0/src/lib.rs:124-125 created: Option<String>; Keyring documentProof.ts:201-213 "vta-sdk verifies a Trust Task proof over a RE-SERIALISATION"
findings.keyringImpact: Keep wireTimestamp, which is cheap and covers older VTAs (I did not check which build the Farm runs). Update the comment. No hcp-specific change.
findings.reasons: HOLDS: The claim holds, and "note" is the right severity. (1) SPEC 4.7: the "What a consumer verifies" paragraph is word-for-word the same at our pin 2a66a0351 (SPEC.md:309), on pr1382 (tt/SPEC.md:310) and on pr1380 (checked with git show pr1380:SPEC.md, line 310). It says "MUST verify a `proof` over the document **as received** … MUST NOT verify over a re-serialization of a typed representation" and names `.000Z` and `+00:00`. (2) VTA at f7b78e29d: `bind_document_to_sender` (mod.rs:1288, cfg didcomm|tsp, "Applied to every document from an intrinsic-sender transport (DIDComm, TSP)") parses `received: Value` from the body and calls `verify_trust_task_proof_value(&received, …)` at mod.rs:1313. It is called from the DIDComm/TSP inbound path (mod.rs:1141) and from collection.rs:540. The claim is, if anything, understated. `dispatch_trust_task_inner` (mod.rs:1452-1456, 1531) records the received JSON for all three transports, REST included, through `received::scope`. The spine's proof check (mod.rs:2051), the step-up gate (step_up.rs:109, on the top-level approve-response), task-consent decisions (task_consent.rs:137) and the mnemonic export (attestation.rs:343) all verify the received form. Every `verify_trust_task_proof_with` (typed) call in vta-service/src that I found is inside a test module (didcomm_bridge.rs:718, webvh_host.rs:829, mod.rs:915/972/5393, consent.rs:1085, step_up.rs:1634). (3) vta-sdk verify.rs:170-185 reads: "# Only for a document this process built (VTI-45) … This form verifies a **re-serialisation** … Every network ingress verifies the received JSON instead, with [`verify_trust_task_proof_value`]." (4) Cargo.lock resolves affinidi-data-integrity 0.8.0, and its lib.rs:125 has `pub created: Option<String>`. `created` is parsed only for the clock-skew check (lib.rs:492-502); the string itself is what gets hashed. (5) Keyring's documentProof.ts:205 still says "vta-sdk verifies a Trust Task proof over a RE-SERIALISATION". It cites verify.rs:144-161, which at the pin is now the typed did:key-only helper, so the comment is out of date for this pin. Two small points that do not change the finding. First, received.rs:18-24 says the typed fallback also covers "a document a handler … extracted itself, a down-converted 0.2 request". In production no handler reaches that fallback with such a document: down-conversion applies only to vault/* specs and happens after the spine's proof check (mod.rs:2149-2151). Second, the as-received verifier at the pin refuses a proof that carries members outside the affinidi model (challenge, domain, expires, id, previousProof) or a null optional proof member (verify.rs:212-228, parse_proof). That does not affect Keyring's timestamp spelling. Which build the Farm runs was not checked, so the claim's keep-wireTimestamp advice still stands.

findings.title: hcp request payloads carry instants that Keyring does not normalize; this is safe only at verifiers that verify as received
findings.claim: The generated Rust hcp types model Instant as chrono DateTime<Utc>, so a typed re-serialization would rewrite payload instants. Request-side instants include audit/read and disclosures/summary from/to; entries/create and entries/revise assertion.validUntil, evidence[].verification.at and record.provenance.assertedAt; grants/revoked revokedAt; shares/report sharedAt; and every instant inside an import's export. Keyring's withWireTimestamps only rewrites top-level issuedAt, expiresAt, validFrom and validUntil.
findings.evidence: trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/hcp/entries/query/v0_1.rs:62 valid_until: Option<chrono::DateTime<Utc>>; grants/request/v0_1.rs:395; scratchpad/sf/instants.py output (entries/create | payload.assertion.validUntil, …); Keyring documentProof.ts:218-231 DATE_TIME_MEMBERS = ['issuedAt','expiresAt','validFrom','validUntil']
findings.keyringImpact: When Keyring builds these payloads, write instants with wireTimestamp (whole seconds, no .000) as well, so they also verify at any verifier that re-serializes.
findings.corrected:
The claim holds and "note" is the right severity. Three details need tightening.

(1) Both cited Rust lines come from response-side types, not request payloads: entries/query/v0_1.rs:62 is Assertion.valid_until and grants/request/v0_1.rs:395 is Grant.expires_at. They show that the generated Rust code models instants as chrono DateTime<Utc>, which is correct. The list of request-side instants comes from the schema walk, and that walk is accurate.

(2) Only the Rust library rewrites instants. The generated Dart library keeps them as strings (for example `final String? validUntil`), and the Go library spot-checked does too (`ValidUntil string` in its non-hcp specs), so a typed round-trip through those libraries changes nothing.

(3) The risk exists only at a verifier that breaks the framework's rules. SPEC.md:310 on the PR branch (line 309 at our pin 2a66a0351) says a consumer "MUST verify a `proof` over the document as received" and "MUST NOT verify over a re-serialization of a typed representation". At VTI f7b78e29d, every network ingress of the VTA verifies the received JSON (verify_trust_task_proof_value, vta-sdk verify.rs:232). The typed form is documented there as "Only for a document this process built (VTI-45)".

The Keyring impact is also slightly mis-worded. wireTimestamp does not produce whole seconds. It only removes a `.000Z` fraction and keeps non-zero milliseconds such as `.123Z`, which chrono writes back unchanged. The accurate wording: when Keyring builds hcp payloads, write every nested instant with wireTimestamp, so that a verifier re-serializing with chrono would still match. This is defence in depth, not an interop requirement.
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: Each part of the claim checks out in source.

- **Rust types:** the generated Rust hcp types use chrono. entries/query/v0_1.rs:62 reads `pub valid_until: ::std::option::Option<::chrono::DateTime<::chrono::offset::Utc>>`, and directives/list/v0_1.rs:466 reads `pub struct Instant(pub ::chrono::DateTime<...Utc>)`. 23 hcp Rust files use DateTime.
- **Request-side instants:** I re-ran the schema walker, read-only, against the pr1382 tree. Its output matches the claim exactly: audit/read and disclosures/summary have from/to; entries/create and entries/revise have assertion.validUntil, evidence[].verification.at and record.provenance.assertedAt; grants/revoked has revokedAt; shares/report has sharedAt; import has its export's exportedAt, audit, delegations, directives and rules instants. The shared Instant is `"type": "string", "format": "date-time"` (common.schema.json:35-38), so nothing in the schema stops a `.000Z` value.
- **Keyring:** documentProof.ts:219 defines `const DATE_TIME_MEMBERS = ['issuedAt', 'expiresAt', 'validFrom', 'validUntil']`. withWireTimestamps (222-231) only touches those top-level members, and only a `.000Z` form. It is applied at :287.

Why this stays a note rather than a raise:
- The framework, on both the PR branch and our pin, forbids verifying over a re-serialization.
- The VTA at the VTI pin verifies the received JSON on network input. The typed path is restricted to documents the VTA built itself.
- The Dart and Go libraries keep instants as strings.

What I corrected:
- The two cited Rust lines are response types, not request payloads.
- "whole seconds" misdescribes wireTimestamp, which keeps non-zero milliseconds.
- "any verifier that re-serializes" really means a chrono-based one.

Side observation outside this claim: the comment at documentProof.ts:205-212 says vta-sdk verifies a re-serialization. At f7b78e29d that is true only of the typed, self-built path.

findings.title: accessTokenDigest's base64url (u) does not clash with Keyring's base58btc (z) digests
findings.claim: accessTokenDigest is something a provider records in a request copy it retains. It appears in no schema and never travels. The framework DigestMultibase accepts z and u, with base58btc RECOMMENDED, identically at our pin and the PR. SPEC 4.9.3 (same at both) requires comparing decoded bytes. task-consent payloadDigest refs that definition, so it accepts both, and Keyring's digestBytesEqual decodes z, u and U.
findings.evidence: specs/hcp/grants/revoke/0.1/spec.md:229 "accessTokenDigest: the SHA-256 multihash of the token's UTF-8 bytes, multibase-encoded as base64url without padding (prefix u)"; no hit for accessTokenDigest in specs/hcp/**/*.json; specs/_framework/0.4/framework.schema.json $defs.DigestMultibase pattern "^(z[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]+|u[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)$", "base58btc is RECOMMENDED"; diff -r of specs/_framework pin vs PR is empty; tt/SPEC.md:558; Keyring documentProof.ts:104-130
findings.keyringImpact: None for wire interop. Keyring never computes accessTokenDigest.
findings.askOfPR: Optional: say why accessTokenDigest fixes u when it calls itself 'the framework's DigestMultibase form', whose recommended base is z, or leave the base to the provider since the record is internal.
findings.corrected:
The claim holds, and "note" is the right severity. A few details are slightly loose:
(1) The same accessTokenDigest sentence, with prefix `u` in every case, appears in 27 hcp/* spec.md files, not only revoke. There are two wordings, a colon or a comma after the name. It appears in no JSON file on pr1380, pr1381 or pr1382, and no response schema (for example audit/read events or the export document) carries a retained request copy.
(2) task-consent/request payloadDigest refs `_framework/0.3/framework.schema.json#/$defs/DigestMultibase`, not 0.4. The 0.3 pattern and description are identical to 0.4's (`^(z…|u…)$`, base58btc RECOMMENDED), so it still accepts both z and u. specs/task-consent is identical at our pin and the PR.
(3) SPEC §4.9.3's decoded-bytes rule is written for verifying a citation (the task digest). Keyring's digestBytesEqual applies it to every comparison: it decodes z through credo, decodes u and U itself, and so is at least as lenient as the rule asks. Keyring's own digestMultibase only ever emits z.
The optional ask stays valid: the text calls `u` "the framework's DigestMultibase form", which is allowed but is not the RECOMMENDED base.
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: I opened every cited location, and each says what the claim says.
- revoke spec.md:229 is under "Retained copies" and says the provider records `accessTokenDigest` "multibase-encoded as base64url without padding (prefix `u`), the framework's `DigestMultibase` form". A provider "MUST remove `accessToken` from the copy it keeps", so the field lives only in a provider-internal record.
- git grep on pr1382, pr1381 and pr1380 finds accessTokenDigest only in spec.md files (27 of them), never in a JSON schema or library file. The export Response is the HCP export document and audit/read returns `events`; neither carries a retained request copy, so the field never travels.
- DigestMultibase has the same pattern and the same "base58btc is RECOMMENDED" text at our pin 2a66a0351 and on the PR branch (in _framework 0.3 and 0.4). `diff -r specs/_framework` between them is empty.
- SPEC.md §4.9.3 is identical at both. Line 558 on the PR says "MUST compare the decoded multihash bytes, not the encoded strings".
- task-consent payloadDigest refs the 0.3 definition, which has the same pattern.
- Keyring documentProof.ts:104-130: decodeMultibaseDigest sends `u` and `U` to decodeBase64Url and everything else (z) to credo MultiBaseEncoder. digestBytesEqual compares the decoded bytes.
- A grep of Keyring's packages and app finds no accessTokenDigest, so Keyring never computes it.
The only imprecisions are which framework version task-consent refs and the fact that the §4.9.3 rule is scoped to citations. Neither changes the conclusion that there is no wire clash.

findings.title: Keyring's consent match code only reads z (base58btc) digests
findings.claim: consentMatchCode decodes payloadDigest with credo's MultiBaseEncoder, which has a decoder only for z. A conforming u (base64url) payloadDigest would show no match code. This affects display only; digestBytesEqual handles u. I did not check which base the VTA's HCP consent producer will use.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/modules/trust-tasks/module/consentCheck.ts:26-38 bytes = MultiBaseEncoder.decode(payloadDigest).data; node_modules/@credo-ts/core/build/utils/MultiBaseEncoder.mjs multibaseDecodingMap = { z: … }
findings.keyringImpact: HCP grant approval reuses task-consent on Keyring (VTI hcp.md:94). Decode u as digestBytesEqual does, so the approver still sees a match code if a producer picks base64url.
findings.corrected: The claim holds; severity stays "note", and the part the claim left unchecked can now be filled in. Keyring's consentMatchCode (consentCheck.ts:26-38) decodes payloadDigest with credo's MultiBaseEncoder. The installed credo 0.7.1-pr-2704 has a decoder only for `z`, and Keyring's yarn patch does not touch it. So a `u` (base64url) digest throws, and the function returns undefined. The only effect is on display: ApprovalDetails.tsx:95 and VtaTrustedApprovers.tsx:1264 hide the code row. The decision still goes out, because isDigestMultibase (vettingShape.ts:119) accepts `u` and the decision echoes the digest string unchanged. The gap is latent against the VTA at f7b78e29d. Both of its consent-digest producers always encode `z`: vti-common/src/task_consent/mod.rs:165 encode_digest_multibase, with the comment "We were already on `z`; keep it, and do not \"generalise\" this to another header", and oob_sign_in.rs grant_digest, through blob_store sha256_digest_multibase (base58btc). VTI hcp.md:94 says HCP grant approval reuses task-consent "as is, with a new producer", and that producer is not written yet. Upstream's own match_code (vta-sdk/src/task_consent.rs:114) uses the generic multibase crate, which also decodes `u`. So if some producer ever chose `u`, upstream approvers would show a code and Keyring would not. Making consentMatchCode decode `u` the way decodeMultibaseDigest already does is a small hardening, not something to ask of the PR.
findings.reasons: HOLDS: Every citation checks out on the right code. Keyring is the d3-fast-send worktree at 5daeba0d0, the VTI clone is at its pin f7b78e29d, and the framework is at our pin 2a66a0351. consentMatchCode calls MultiBaseEncoder.decode(payloadDigest).data inside a try/catch that returns undefined. credo's multibaseDecodingMap contains only `z`, and decode throws "No decoder found for multibase prefix" for anything else. digestBytesEqual goes through decodeMultibaseDigest, which handles `u`/`U` itself and leaves the rest to credo, so "digestBytesEqual handles u" is correct. The framework allows both bases (SPEC.md:2195: "`DigestMultibase` admits both base58btc and base64url"), so a conforming `u` producer is possible. "Display only" is also correct: the UI hides the code row when there is no code, and the decision path accepts `u` and echoes the string. Where the claim said "I did not check", I checked: every existing VTA consent-digest producer encodes `z` and has comments saying to keep it, so the gap cannot be reached from the VTA today. That keeps it a "note".

findings.title: Framework 0.6.0 is older than our pin's text; no envelope or proof rule changed between the pin and the PR
findings.claim: The hcp specs target framework 0.6.0. Our pin's SPEC.md already has the 0.7.0 changelog, and its specs/_framework (including 0.6/trust-task.schema.json) is identical to the PR's. The SPEC.md diff from the pin to the PR only adds §4.13 Trust Ceremonies, rewords ceremony terms, adds a producer rule for evidence answering a held next-step, and restates decline handling in §8.6. The members in §4.2, proof §4.7, suites §4.7.1, purpose §4.7.3 and digests §4.9.3 are unchanged. The PR also does not touch the proof libraries.
findings.evidence: specs/hcp/entries/query/0.1/spec.md:7 targetFrameworkVersion: "0.6.0"; pin external/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/SPEC.md:2016 "### B.1 Framework version 0.7.0"; git diff 2a66a0351 HEAD -- SPEC.md (127+/8-, hunks at 4.13 and ceremony text only); tt/SPEC.md:1122 new producer rule; git diff --stat origin/main pr1380 -- SPEC.md trust-tasks-ts-proof/src trust-tasks-proof/src is empty
findings.keyringImpact: No pin bump is needed for envelope or proof reasons.
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: The main claim holds. Every cited quote checks out at the right commit (PR head e163cac on pr1382, which equals origin/feat/hcp-demos, and the pin 2a66a0351): 28 of 28 specs give 0.6.0, the pin's SPEC.md:2016 reads "### B.1 Framework version 0.7.0", `git diff --stat 2a66a0351 pr1382 -- specs/_framework` is empty, the SPEC.md diff is 127+/8- with no hunk in §4.2's member list or §4.7 to §4.9.3, and the line at SPEC.md:1122 is the new producer rule. The pin is an ancestor of the PR branch, and SPEC.md, the framework schemas and the proof sources match between origin/main and pr1380/pr1382, so the PR's own diff leaves all three alone.

The claim is overstated in one place. Its evidence for the proof libraries compares origin/main with the PR, not the pin with the PR. Between the pin and the PR, the TS, Rust and Dart proof libraries changed their verification behaviour (#1168, #1233, #1210, #1167, #1204, all merged after 2026-11-10). These commits say they enforce rules already in SPEC §4.7.3 and in the JCS cryptosuite spec, so no framework rule changed, but the reference behaviour did. Two smaller points: the §8.6 change is a real change to how a decline is handled, not a restatement, and §4.2's `ceremony` row was reworded. Neither touches the envelope or proofs.

findings.title: hcp documents use the same envelope Keyring sends to the VTA
findings.claim: hcp documents use the framework 0.6 envelope unchanged. The 0.6 envelope schema requires id, type and payload and allows additional top-level members, and the hcp parties require issuer and recipient. Keyring's VtaClient sends id (urn:uuid), type, threadId (a fresh urn:uuid, allowed to differ from id), payload, issuer, recipient (the VTA DID), issuedAt, top-level extras covered by the proof, and a proof with an absolute verificationMethod. The type may carry #request or no fragment; the two are equivalent. The VTA binds issuer == proof signer == transport sender.
findings.evidence: specs/_framework/0.6/trust-task.schema.json required ['id','type','payload'], additionalProperties true; tt/SPEC.md:209 rule 1 (no fragment and #request equivalent); transcript.golden.txt:88 type …/grants/request/0.1#request; Keyring VtaClient.ts:1919-1933; vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs:1288-1320
findings.keyringImpact: No envelope change. One thing to watch: provider-side matching of a grants/request resubmit is by threadId + issuer (grants/request/0.1/spec.md:175), and VtaClient mints a new threadId per send. That matters only if the Context Client code reuses VtaClient (unverified).
findings.corrected:
Severity stays ok for the envelope's shape, but the Keyring impact is too narrow. The shape claim holds. Every hcp spec targets framework 0.6.0. The 0.6 envelope schema requires only id, type and payload, sets additionalProperties to true, and is byte-identical at our pin 2a66a0351 and on pr1382. All 28 hcp specs mark both issuer and recipient REQUIRED. Keyring's VtaClient.sendTask builds id (urn:uuid), type, a fresh urn:uuid threadId (SPEC 4.9: producers "MAY mint a fresh value"), payload, issuer, recipient = vtaDid, issuedAt, and signed top-level extras. It signs with an absolute verificationMethod (documentProof.ts:275-277). A bare type and #request are equivalent (SPEC.md:209), and the VTA's trust-tasks-rs 0.37.2 for_routing() treats them as one. Over DIDComm and TSP the VTA requires issuer == proof signer == transport sender (mod.rs:1314-1315). One exception: a public task sent without a proof is let through unbound (mod.rs:1302-1306).

Two corrections to the impact. (1) The watch item is not only threadId reuse by a Context Client. In hcp/entries/create, revise and hard-delete, HCP's idempotency key is the document id ("`Idempotency-Key` header (HCP 9.6) | the document `id`", entries/create/0.1/spec.md:117; repeated requests at :250-252). VTI #2823's design has Keyring itself send hcp/entries/create as a V0 governance task (hcp.md:232-233). VtaClient mints a new document id on every send (VtaClient.ts:1917), and handles retries with a top-level idempotencyKey member that the hcp specs never define. So if Keyring retries a create after the answer was lost, it must resend the same id. Otherwise a provider that follows the hcp spec creates a second entry. Severity: note (our own code; no ask of the PR). (2) Minor, no break: the hcp spec examples sign with proofPurpose "assertionMethod" (47 times, e.g. grants/request/0.1/spec.md:163). Keyring signs hcp requests for "authentication" (proofPurpose.ts), as do the demo transcript and the framework's SHOULD (SPEC.md:374). No hcp spec requires a purpose, so this is compatible; at most, a request to make the examples consistent.
findings.reasons: HOLDS: Every cited location says what the claim says, on the right branch and pin. Schema: specs/_framework/0.6/trust-task.schema.json has "required": ["id","type","payload"] and "additionalProperties": true, unchanged between our pin and pr1382. SPEC.md:209: "carries no fragment or the fragment #request is a request. The two forms are semantically equivalent". transcript.golden.txt:88 has "type": "https://trusttasks.org/spec/hcp/grants/request/0.1#request". VtaClient.ts:1919-1933 builds exactly the listed members, with threadId and documentId minted fresh at :1916-1917. vta-service mod.rs:1314-1315: "Some(issuer) if issuer == signer && issuer == sender => Ok(())". grants/request/0.1/spec.md:175 confirms matching on (threadId, issuer). So the claim is not refuted. It is only understated: the stated Keyring impact misses that hcp's mutating entry tasks use the document id as the idempotency key, which conflicts with VtaClient's fresh id per send. That matters for Keyring as Management Client, since the VTI design names it as the sender of hcp/entries/create. It is not only a Context Client concern.

findings.title: ext["vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage"] passes Keyring's checks; request payloads are closed
findings.claim: The namespace appears only in the hcp/import response. That response's ext is a $ref to the framework Ext (any reverse-DNS key), so Keyring's Ajv passes it, VtaClient casts and ignores it, and framework rule 5 says to ignore an unknown namespace. Its inner shape is only an uncheckedRule (#1381), not a schema check. Every hcp request schema I checked has additionalProperties false, so Keyring cannot add ext to a request. The vnd.trusttasks. prefix has registry precedent.
findings.evidence: specs/hcp/import/0.1/payload.schema.json:54,209-213; spec.md:345; $defs.Response.properties.ext = {"$ref": "../../../_framework/0.4/framework.schema.json#/$defs/Ext"}; pr1381 import spec.md:90 uncheckedRule; specs/did-management/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md:59 "vnd.trusttasks.did-method-webvh"
findings.keyringImpact: None. If Keyring later shows delegate imports, read rulesNotApplied from that namespace.
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: The claim holds on every point I checked, and "ok" is the right severity.

(1) The namespace appears in only one place. In all three PR branches (pr1380/1381/1382) `vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage` shows up only in the hcp/import spec and schema, the drift allowlist and the generated libraries. It is not in examples/hcp-demo-ts, not in ceremonies, and not in the VTI #2823 design docs.

(2) The schema does not check it. In import payload.schema.json:52-54, `ext` is just {"$ref": "../../../_framework/0.4/framework.schema.json#/$defs/Ext"}. Ext (framework.schema.json) is type object, minProperties 1, additionalProperties true, with propertyNames ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$. `HcpCarriageImportExtension` (lines 207-213) is defined but nothing references it. The generated TS RESPONSE_PAYLOAD_SCHEMA inlines Ext and leaves it out (trust-tasks-ts/src/hcp/import/0.1/payload.ts:1466-1515).

(3) Keyring's Ajv accepts it. I ran Keyring's Ajv2020 ({strict:false}, the same setup as validator.ts:15) on the import Response with Ext inlined:
- a correct carriage value passes;
- a junk inner value {foo:1} also passes, so the inner shape is not checked;
- a bare key `hcpCarriage` fails (control);
- `rulesNotApplied` placed beside `outcomes` fails on additionalProperties (control);
- a request carrying `ext` fails on additionalProperties.

(4) The inner shape is an uncheckedRule only on pr1381. pr1381 import spec.md:90 reads "Where present, `ext[\"vnd.trusttasks.hcp-carriage\"]` validates against the `HcpCarriageImportExtension` definition". On pr1382 the MUST is in prose at spec.md:345, plus "a Management Client that does not recognize the namespace ignores it".

(5) Framework rule 5 matches, at both the PR branch and our pin 2a66a0351. SPEC.md:247 reads "A consumer MUST ignore namespaces it does not recognize ... except where the namespace is named critical". The import Response has no `extCritical` property and is additionalProperties false, so the namespace can never be marked critical.

(6) Every request is closed. I scanned all 28 hcp payload schemas (on pr1382, and on the pr1380 worktree too). Each has a top-level additionalProperties false, and none has an `ext` property anywhere except import's $defs/Response. The _shared schemas have none either.

(7) The registry precedent is real. specs/did-management/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md:59 has `"vnd.trusttasks.did-method-webvh": {`, also at our pin, with its own extension schema in did-method-extensions/webvh.schema.json.

Two points of precision, neither enough to refute:
- Keyring's Ajv does not run on VTA replies today. VtaClient.sendTask ends `return (body?.payload ?? body) as T` (VtaClient.ts:2110), and trustTaskPayloadValidator is used only by TrustTasksService, vettingShape and the witness server. So "Ajv passes it" is what would happen if a future hcp client validated the reply against the published schema. "VtaClient casts and ignores it" is literally true.
- "Cannot add ext to a request" means the framework `ext` member. HCP-owned open objects inside requests (ImportedExport, entries, Outcome and others with additionalProperties true) still accept arbitrary members, but those are not framework `ext`.

Since the schema never checks the inner shape, a Management Client that reads rulesNotApplied must check its shape itself.

findings.title: V0 says Keyring sends governance tasks with no token, but every Management Client schema requires accessToken
findings.claim: The VTI design (PR #2823) and our plan's companion decision D2 have Keyring authenticate the V0 governance tasks (grants/revoke, audit/read, disclosures/summary, entries/create) as the admin DID, with no token. Every one of those request schemas lists accessToken as required (string, minLength 1) and is closed (additionalProperties false). So does every other Management Client request schema I checked: grants/list, export, import, restrict-purposes. A document without a token fails SPEC 7.2 item 2 at any validating consumer, including the VTA spine, and neither design says what goes in accessToken.
findings.evidence: vti2823/docs/05-design-notes/hcp.md:158 "Keyring → VTA | DIDComm authcrypt from the admin DID, a required document proof by that DID, the ACL admin role; no token (§4.4)"; hcp.md:230-239; agent-connect-plan/2026-11-25-bam.md:450 "D2 … Keyring has no VTA session token"; specs/hcp/grants/revoke/0.1/payload.schema.json required ['grantId','accessToken'], accessToken {type string, minLength 1, maxLength 8192}, additionalProperties False (same pattern in audit/read, disclosures/summary, entries/create)
findings.keyringImpact: Keyring cannot send a schema-valid revoke, audit or summary request without some accessToken value. Either Keyring gets a management token (moving VTI's V1 item forward), or the demo VTA skips payload validation for these tasks, which does not conform. This has to be decided before Keyring's side of the demo is built.
findings.askOfPR: Brendan (VTI #2823): what does Keyring put in accessToken for the V0 governance tasks? Should the VTA issue a management token at setup (as the demo's MANAGEMENT_TOKEN does) instead of relying on the admin DID with no token?
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: The claim holds. Every quote is accurate, comes from the right branch or pin, and supports the conclusion. Severity "raise" is right: VTI controls both sides and can fix it cheaply, but Keyring's V0 side cannot be built schema-valid until someone decides what goes in accessToken.

All CONFIRMED by reading the source:

(1) VTI #2823 says Keyring sends no token. hcp.md:158 says "...the ACL admin role; no token (§4.4)". hcp.md:230-239 names the four governance tasks, says they authenticate "the **admin DID**", and says "V1 adds dedicated opaque management tokens". The same position appears in hcp.md:551 (decision 7), hcp-tasks.md:165, hcp-plan.md:132 and tasks/hcp-demo-plan.md:171-172. None of these files mentions accessToken for Keyring's path. The divergence table (hcp.md:591) records only a departure from "HCP 1.6, 5.4". It does not record a departure from the suite's required payload member.

(2) Our companion's D2 says the same. agent-connect-plan/2026-11-25-bam.md:450: "Keyring has no VTA session token. As Management Client it authenticates as the administrator DID...". Neither the companion nor agent-connect-plan.md mentions accessToken for Keyring's tasks.

(3) The schemas require the token. On pr1382, grants/revoke, audit/read, disclosures/summary, entries/create, grants/list, export, import and entries/restrict-purposes all have accessToken in `required`, typed {string, minLength 1, maxLength 8192}, with `additionalProperties: false`. In fact every hcp/* request schema does; the provider-sent notice grants/revoked has no accessToken at all.

(4) SPEC.md:1132 (§7.2 item 2) requires a consumer to validate the payload against its schema. SPEC.md:1115 (§7.1 item 3) also makes a producer that sends no token non-conforming.

(5) The VTA spine would reject such a request; this is a design consequence, not live behaviour today. At VTI pin f7b78e29d, `validate_payload` (vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs:605-632) checks every type with a published schema. It runs before the policy gate and outside `policy.enforcement` (mod.rs:1967-1988), and only ceremony tasks are exempt. The hcp schemas are not in that index at the pin (no vti-specs-hcp crate yet). But hcp.md:24 says "V0 pins the family as frozen at X0", and hcp-tasks.md:81 (task A1) pins it in vti-specs-hcp.

(6) The suite's authorization model conflicts with V0's design, not only its schema. specs/hcp/grants/revoke/0.1/spec.md:87 says the authority "is evidenced by the Management Client's access token in `accessToken`". spec.md:91 says of the proof: "It is not the authorization: the token is." SPEC §7.2 item 10 lets a proof count as authorization only where the task spec defines it so, and this one does not.

(7) The suite's own demo already does what the ask suggests. tt/examples/hcp-demo-ts/src/demo.ts:111 defines `MANAGEMENT_TOKEN = "hcp_mt_demo_management"; // DEMO ONLY: issued to the person's app at setup`, and :311 refuses a revoke whose token differs.

One small imprecision: hcp/entries/create is not an HCP governance operation. It is a context-plane write (HCP 5.2.3). Its spec gives the role as "a Context Client, or a Management Client" (spec.md:16), and its token is "the HCP access token that stands for the grant". The label "governance" is VTI's, and the claim inherits it. It still requires accessToken, so the conclusion is unchanged. || HOLDS: I found nothing that contradicts the claim, and every part of it checks out (CONFIRMED). 1) Schemas: I scanned all 28 hcp/* payload.schema.json files on pr1382. The top-level request schema of every task whose role is Management Client, or HCP Client with Management Client as an option, requires accessToken and sets additionalProperties false. For the eight named tasks (grants/revoke, audit/read, disclosures/summary, entries/create, grants/list, export, import, entries/restrict-purposes) accessToken is {type string, minLength 1}. Only grants/request (where the token is in the Response), grants/revoked and the Context-Client-only tasks differ. pr1381 does not change this: its revoke schema still has required ['grantId','accessToken'] and additionalProperties False. 2) No exception in the suite: the specs say the proof "is not the authorization: the token is" (revoke :91, audit/read :109, disclosures/summary :101). entries/create :99 goes further: "The authority is **the grant** … evidenced by the access token", with authorizedUnder "still taken from the grant" (:101). So for entries/create even a management token may not be enough. No hcp spec allows ACL or transport identity in place of the token. 3) The VTA spine at f7b78e29d validates whenever the schema is pinned: mod.rs:605-651 validate_payload refuses with MalformedRequest "payload does not conform", and it is called at :1986 "deliberately not behind `policy.enforcement`". Only ceremony tasks are exempt. A1 pins the hcp/* tasks into vti-specs-hcp, so a revoke without a token is refused before any handler runs. 4) SPEC.md 7.2 item 2 requires validating payload against the type's schema. 5) Neither design fills the gap: hcp.md §4.4 (:230-239) and §12 record the divergence only from "HCP 1.6, 5.4", not from the suite's required member. hcp-plan.md, hcp-tasks.md (A4-A6, A8 :165 "no token"), hcp-demo-plan.md:171-172 and the Keyring companion (D2 :450; it mentions accessToken only for the CLI, :34/:108/:188) never say what Keyring puts in accessToken. 6) The suite's own demo does what the ask suggests: examples/hcp-demo-ts/src/demo.ts:111 MANAGEMENT_TOKEN "issued to the person's app at setup", checked at :311 and sent in revoke at :585. Severity "raise" is right, not blocker: we and Brendan control both sides, and the fix (a demo management token) is cheap. Keyring's C track should still not be built until it is decided. Keyring's existing accessToken in VtiMediatorTransport.ts:623 is a mediator login token and has nothing to do with this.

findings.title: Regenerated Go and Dart types drop required-nullable nulls, so they emit documents the PR's own schemas refuse
findings.claim: In the libraries regenerated in #1380, a required-and-nullable member set to null is omitted on serialization in Go (pointer with omitempty) and in Dart (if != null). Example: a persistent grant's expiresAt, or a Management Client query response's directives. The schema lists those members as required, so the output fails payload validation. Rust (Option without skip_serializing_if) and TS keep the null. Fix branches exist but are not in #1380's generated code.
findings.evidence: trust-tasks-go/specs/hcp/grants/request/v0_1/payload.go:177 ExpiresAt *string `json:"expiresAt,omitempty"`; trust-tasks-go/specs/hcp/entries/query/v0_1/payload.go:41 Directives *[]Directive `json:"directives,omitempty"`; trust-tasks-dart/lib/specs/hcp/grants/request/v0_1/payload.dart:716 if (expiresAt != null) 'expiresAt': expiresAt!; specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/grant.schema.json:10 required includes "expiresAt"; trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/hcp/grants/request/v0_1.rs:393-395; origin/fix/go-required-nullable 21f75e283, origin/fix/dart-required-nullable 43f7a00a2
findings.keyringImpact: No direct impact on Keyring, which talks to the Rust VTA. A Go or Dart HCP provider or client would hand Keyring responses missing required members.
findings.askOfPR: Regenerate #1380 after #1374-#1379 land, and add a conformance case for a persistent grant (expiresAt null) and a Management Client query (directives null) in each language.
findings.corrected:
The claim holds, and raise is the right severity, but it needs one addition: #1380 already admits this defect. In the libraries regenerated on pr1380 (94ed4200c; pr1382 has the same Go and Dart hcp code), Go drops the key when a required nullable member is nil, because the field is a pointer tagged omitempty: grants/request/v0_1/payload.go:177 `ExpiresAt *string json:"expiresAt,omitempty"` and entries/query/v0_1/payload.go:41 `Directives *[]Directive json:"directives,omitempty"`. Dart does the same through `if (x != null)` in toJson: grants/request/v0_1/payload.dart:716, shared/v0_1/grant.dart:519, entries/query/v0_1/payload.dart:1668. The schemas require both members and allow null: grant.schema.json:10 for expiresAt, and query payload.schema.json $defs/Response for directives, typed ["array","null"]. So a persistent grant, or a query answered to a client that is not a Context Client (such as a Management Client), comes out of Go or Dart as a document its own schema rejects. Rust keeps the null: v0_1.rs:393-395 has no skip_serializing_if, and query v0_1.rs:4596 is the same. TS keeps it too: `expiresAt: string | null` in _shared/components.ts, and `directives: Directive[] | null` at query payload.ts:297.

The addition: the PR's own docs/runtime-parity.md:73 already says "A required nullable member set to null is left out, and the document fails its own schema" for both Go and Dart. That row also lists more affected hcp members than the two examples: Grant.expiresAt, DelegationTerm.endsAt, usableUntil, permittedPurposes, five AuditEvent members, and the get and query directives. The fixes are open PRs, not yet in pr1380 or main: #1378 (fix/go-required-nullable, 21f75e283), which drops omitempty from required members in emit.go and build-go-bindings.mjs, and #1379 (fix/dart-required-nullable, 43f7a00a2). The parity row's Dart entry, "not yet planned", is out of date now that #1379 exists.

The ask should be: merge #1378 and #1379 before #1380, regenerate #1380's Go and Dart hcp code, update parity row 73, and add a test in each language with a null for every required nullable hcp member the row lists, not only expiresAt and directives. Severity: raise. Keyring impact: none directly. | The claim holds, at severity raise, but needs four corrections. (1) The PR already knows about it: #1380 adds docs/runtime-parity.md:73, which says for Go "A required nullable member set to null is left out, and the document fails its own schema" and says the same for Dart ("null is left out, required members included (for example `expiresAt`…)"). The row is marked "todo", and its Dart line, "Dart: not yet planned", is out of date now that origin/fix/dart-required-nullable exists. (2) #1380 did not introduce the bug. It sits in the generators that are already on main: scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs:875 `const tag = isRequired && !nullable ? wireName : \`${wireName},omitempty\``, the Go per-module generator cmd/trust-tasks-gen/emit.go:480-482 (same rule, so moving to generating your own packages does not escape it), and the Dart toJson emitter. The fix branches also regenerate non-HCP specs on main (vta/contexts/update-did 1.1/1.2, vtc/vetting/hidden publish/show/withdraw). Neither fix branch is an ancestor of origin/main or pr1380. (3) It reaches further than the two examples. Eleven required, nullable members in specs/hcp hit it: Grant.expiresAt; five AuditEvent members; DelegationTerm.endsAt; disclosures/summary usableUntil; entries/get and entries/query directives; and a REQUEST member, entries/restrict-purposes permittedPurposes, where null means "remove the narrowing". That request is sent by a Management Client, and in Go (payload.go:448) and Dart (payload.dart:216) it loses that null too. (4) Go does not check payloads before sending (RespondWith, document.go:598, builds the document without validating), so the bad document does go out, and only a receiver that validates it refuses it. The Go demo never sets either value to null (demo.go:605 `ExpiresAt: &expiresAt`, :671 `Directives: &directives`), which is why nothing has caught it. The ask should be: close the documented todo before the hcp Go/Dart packages ship, by landing the fixes and regenerating (the Dart fix is breaking, `fix(dart)!`), and add conformance cases with null for expiresAt, directives and permittedPurposes in each language. Keyring is not directly affected: it is TypeScript, and JSON.stringify keeps nulls.
findings.reasons: HOLDS: I opened every cited file:line on pr1380 (94ed4200c), and each one says what the claim says. pr1382's Go and Dart hcp code is identical (an empty diff against pr1380). Two schema-side facts back the conclusion. First, both members are listed as required and allow null. Second, the Go and Dart encoders really do leave a nil or null member out: omitempty on a pointer, and `if != null` in toJson. Neither library has a custom MarshalJSON for these types, and Go's payload validator runs when a document is received, so a schema-checking receiver would reject the document. Rust and TS keep the null. The fix branches exist (#1378 Go and #1379 Dart, both open per gh), and git merge-base --is-ancestor shows neither is in pr1380, pr1382 or main. What makes the claim incomplete rather than wrong is that the PR's own runtime-parity.md:73 already states this defect and lists more affected members. || HOLDS: I looked for anything that would contradict the claim and found nothing. On pr1380, both Go generators tag a required, nullable member with `omitempty`, which drops a nil pointer from the output. Dart writes such a member only `if (x != null)`. The schema lists expiresAt and directives as required with type [..., "null"], and HCP's own grant.json does the same. Rust's Option has no skip_serializing_if, so it keeps the null. No checked Go type or option writes the null, and Go does not check payloads on send. The demos never exercise the null case. The claim is accurate but understated in scope, and it misses three things: the PR's own runtime-parity.md already lists the defect as a todo, the defect comes from generators already on main, and it also affects a Management Client request (restrict-purposes permittedPurposes). Raise remains the right severity.

findings.title: Required-and-nullable hcp members, and the JS undefined trap
findings.claim: Required and nullable: AuditEvent.entryId, relatedEntryId, purpose, purposeDescription and grantId; DelegationTerm.endsAt; Grant.expiresAt; disclosures/summary ClientSummary.usableUntil; entries/get and entries/query Response.directives; and entries/restrict-purposes request permittedPurposes, which Keyring sends (null removes the narrowing). Keyring's Ajv refuses an absent required-nullable member, but JSON.stringify turns an undefined value into an absent member. nextCursor is the reverse: absent, never null, unlike HCP 9.5.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/sf/nullable.py output (REQUIRED+nullable _shared/0.1/grant.schema.json #Grant/expiresAt …); specs/hcp/entries/restrict-purposes/0.1/payload.schema.json required ['entryId','permittedPurposes','expectedVersion','accessToken'], permittedPurposes type ["array","null"]; disclosures/summary/0.1/payload.schema.json:61-65 "Absent, never null … a departure from HCP 9.5's null"; scratchpad/sf/ajvfmt.cjs: "absent required-nullable accepted: false", JSON.stringify({p: undefined}) → {}
findings.keyringImpact: Keyring code must write an explicit null for permittedPurposes, and must read directives: null and expiresAt: null without treating them as absent.
findings.corrected: The claim holds, at severity note. One word is too strong: "which Keyring sends". No Keyring code sends any hcp/* task today (a grep of d3-fast-send's packages/trust-tasks/src, packages/core/src and app/src finds nothing). restrict-purposes is a Management Client task, so as the Management Client Keyring would be its only sender, but it is planned for P2/V2 (companion 2026-11-25-bam.md:387), not built. Precise version: on all three PR branches (#1380, #1381 and #1382 have identical schemas), exactly ten members are required and nullable. They are AuditEvent.entryId, relatedEntryId, purpose, purposeDescription and grantId; DelegationTerm.endsAt; Grant.expiresAt; ClientSummary.usableUntil; Response.directives in entries/get and in entries/query; and the restrict-purposes request's permittedPurposes. Six of them (the five AuditEvent members and directives) are required by the carriage although HCP's own shape leaves them optional (questions 42 and 5). Keyring's Ajv2020 refuses a required-nullable member that is absent. It also refuses one whose value is undefined in memory, so the trap bites before JSON.stringify drops the key as well. nextCursor in audit/read, disclosures/summary and grants/list is optional and string-only: absent, never null, while HCP 9.5 (written for GET /v2/audit) sends null.
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: I re-checked every point myself rather than trusting the cited scratchpad output.

1. My own census script, which handles type arrays, anyOf/oneOf, and enum/const null and follows $refs, finds the same ten required-and-nullable members on pr1382 (e163cac) and on pr1380 (94ed420). `git diff` shows no schema.json changes between pr1380, pr1381 and pr1382.

2. Cited quotes:
   - restrict-purposes:8 is `"required": ["entryId", "permittedPurposes", "expectedVersion", "accessToken"]`, and :15 is `"type": ["array", "null"]`. Its description says "Null removes the Authorizing Principal's narrowing (HCP 9.4.10)".
   - disclosures/summary:61-65 says "Absent, never null, when the result set is exhausted or the provider does not paginate: a departure from HCP 9.5's null".
   - audit/read:71 and grants/list:55 say the same.
   - HCP spec b790561, specification.md:2400, says "Responses carry a `nextCursor` member holding an opaque token, or null when the result set is exhausted."

3. Keyring's validator (validator.ts:15, `new Ajv2020({ strict: false })`) was run against the real PR restrict-purposes schema with a control:
   - a list is accepted (control);
   - null is accepted;
   - absent is refused ("must have required property 'permittedPurposes'");
   - an in-memory undefined is refused;
   - an undefined after a JSON round-trip is refused;
   - JSON.stringify drops the key.
   For Grant, expiresAt: null is accepted and absent is refused.

The only overstatement is the present tense of "Keyring sends". The impact on Keyring and the severity (note) are right.

Side observation, outside this finding: restrict-purposes' $id has no file name (`.../restrict-purposes/0.1`), so plain Ajv resolves `../../../_shared/` to `/spec/_shared/` rather than `/spec/hcp/_shared/`. That is harmless only where refs are inlined first, which is what Keyring's validator expects.

findings.title: Keyring does not validate or enforce VTA reply payloads and proofs
findings.claim: Peer documents consumed through TrustTasksService are checked against their payload schema with Ajv. VTA replies are not: VtaClient.sendTask casts the payload, and only logs the proof verdict, refusing nothing. For the 12 hcp specs whose response proof is REQUIRED, an unsigned or badly signed response would still be used, against SPEC 7.2 item 7. Separately, Keyring's Ajv (strict false, no ajv-formats) ignores format date-time and uri.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/modules/trust-tasks/module/VtaClient.ts:2093 void checkVtaReply(…).then(… logger.warn …); :2110 return (body?.payload ?? body) as T; services/TrustTasksService.ts:105 payloadPolicy: { kind: 'validate', … }; packages/trust-tasks/src/validator.ts:15 new Ajv2020({ strict: false }); scratchpad/sf/ajvfmt.cjs: 'unknown format "date-time" ignored', 'bad date-time and bad uri accepted: true'
findings.keyringImpact: Before Keyring relies on hcp responses (grants, disclosures summary, audit), add schema validation for hcp reply payloads. Refuse replies whose required proof is missing or does not verify. Add ajv-formats if the format checks are wanted.
findings.corrected:
The claim holds as written. Two small corrections. (1) Severity: this is work Keyring has to do itself and the finding makes no ask of the PR, so under this review's scale it is a "note" (a Keyring action item before it consumes hcp responses), not a "raise". (2) In the Keyring-impact line, "grants" is too broad. Only grants/request has a REQUIRED response proof. grants/list, read-own, relinquish, revoke and revoked are RECOMMENDED. The 12 REQUIRED ones are audit/read, delegations/list, disclosures/summary, entries/{confirm,create,get,query,restrict-purposes,revise,set-categories}, export and grants/request. Context worth keeping: the gap is in VtaClient.sendTask only. Other reply paths already refuse unverified documents: foreignApproval.readReply throws unless checkVtaReply says verified, and vtiVetting.openPeerDocument refuses a proof that is missing or does not verify. VTA replies also arrive over an authenticated DIDComm or TSP session, so the real risk is lower, but the SPEC 7.2 item 7 refusal is still not met. | The core claim holds. Keyring's general VTA reply path, VtaClient.sendTask, does not check reply payloads against a schema. It checks the proof only off the answer's path and refuses nothing. The code says so (VtaClient.ts:2092 "refuses nothing yet"), and the payload is returned as a plain cast (:2110). Keyring has no hcp/* code yet, so this is a gap to close before C3 entries/create, C4 audit/read and disclosures/summary are built on sendTask. Those three are among the 12 specs whose proofRequirement.response is REQUIRED (I confirmed 12 by frontmatter).

Three corrections:
(a) The scope is VtaClient.sendTask replies only. Other VTA and peer documents are checked and refused: VTA-signed consent requests (consentCheck.ts:91), a foreign agent's reply (foreignApproval.ts:141-143 throws unless verified), and vetting documents (vtiVetting.ts openPeerDocument plus the vettingShape schema checks).
(b) SPEC §7.2 item 7 asks for more than the claim says. Any response that carries a proof must be verified and refused with proofInvalid if it fails, including the RECOMMENDED-proof hcp responses. The REQUIRED status of the 12 specs only adds the proofRequired refusal when the proof is missing.
(c) JSON Schema 2020-12 treats `format` as annotation-only by default, so Keyring ignoring it is allowed. But the PR's own TS demo validator (examples/hcp-demo-ts/src/validator.ts:19, addFormats(new Ajv2020(...))) enforces formats, so Keyring would accept date-time and uri values the reference refuses.

Severity: the finding has no ask of the PR and is a Keyring-side to-do. By the review's own scale it fits "note" (a Keyring action item) better than "raise".
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: I read every cited line at d3-fast-send 5daeba0d0, and each says what the claim says. VtaClient.ts:2090-2092 comments "Keyring logs the verdict first, off the answer's path, and refuses nothing yet". At :2093 a `void checkVtaReply(...)` only calls logger.info or logger.warn. At :2110 `return (body?.payload ?? body) as T` returns the reply with no Ajv or schema check. The only refusals on this path are a DIDComm problem-report (:2086) and a trust-task-error type (:2106). TrustTasksService.ts:105 has `payloadPolicy: { kind: 'validate', validate: trustTaskPayloadValidator }` for documents run through consume(), and most callers also pass a real proof policy (proofUnder, issueProofPolicy). validator.ts:15 is `new Ajv2020({ strict: false })`. No addFormats or ajv-formats exists anywhere in non-test code; only roomsDataPath.test.ts adds formats. I ran the same Ajv setup with the installed ajv 8.20.0 and got 'unknown format "date-time" ignored' and 'unknown format "uri" ignored', and bad values were accepted (true). The hcp _shared schemas do use format uri and date-time (common.schema.json:14,29,37). The proofRequirement front matter on the pr1382 branch gives response: REQUIRED on exactly 12 of the 28 hcp specs. SPEC 7.2 item 7 says to reject with proofInvalid or proofRequired, both on the PR branch (SPEC.md:1136) and at our pin 2a66a0351 (SPEC.md:1017). Nothing in the claim is misread or from the wrong version. The only issues are the severity and the "grants" wording. || HOLDS: I looked for counter-evidence and found none that defeats the claim.

- There is no switch or plan to enforce reply proofs. The only grep hit is the "refuses nothing yet" comment itself.
- Neither the agent-connect plan nor its HCP companion commits to checking reply proofs or reply schemas.
- TrustTasksService does validate, but it is used only for inbound consume, not for VtaClient answers.
- No ajv-formats is installed or imported in Keyring's runtime code. A Keyring test file even notes it (pcsVtaPayloads.test.ts:61, "the shared schemas use formats ajv does not know without ajv-formats").
- Re-run with Keyring's own ajv 8.20.0, `new Ajv2020({ strict: false })` printed 'unknown format "date-time" ignored' and accepted a bad date-time and a bad uri.

What I did find only narrows the claim: other Keyring paths do verify and refuse, SPEC §7.2 item 7 covers more responses than the claim says, and format checking is optional in JSON Schema 2020-12. Severity is better as "note", since nothing is asked of the PR.

findings.title: Keyring's VTA reply verifier does not bind the key to its relationship and accepts keyAgreement
findings.claim: verifyTrustTaskProof finds the method in verificationMethod, authentication or assertionMethod, whatever proofPurpose says, and accepts any non-empty purpose, including keyAgreement. Its doc says upstream does the same, but vta-sdk at f7b78e29d binds the purpose to the DID relationship (VTI-KEY-022) and refuses keyAgreement, and SPEC 4.7.3 makes that a MUST. Separately, verifyDocumentProof's default refuses anything not signed assertionMethod, so pointed at a VTA- or PR-signed hcp document it returns false.
findings.evidence: packages/trust-tasks/src/documentProof.ts:532-536 "What it does NOT check, deliberately, as upstream does not: which proofPurpose"; :550 checks only non-empty; :568-573 method lookup ignores purpose; :453 if (p.proofPurpose !== (requiredPurpose ?? 'assertionMethod')) return false; vta-sdk/src/trust_task_proof/verify.rs:313-316; purpose.rs:81-94; tt/SPEC.md:374 and §4.7.3 items 1-3
findings.keyringImpact: Bring verifyTrustTaskProof up to the pin's vta-sdk: bind the method to the relationship named by proofPurpose, and refuse keyAgreement and unknown values. Never use verifyDocumentProof's default on hcp documents.
findings.corrected:
The claim holds, with three corrections.

1. The core claim is right. At Keyring origin/main (c65701c91, same text as d3-fast-send), `verifyTrustTaskProof`, which `checkVtaReply` in vtaReplyProof.ts uses for VTA replies, accepts any non-empty proofPurpose, including keyAgreement. It looks the method up in `verificationMethod` plus any methods embedded under `authentication` or `assertionMethod`, whatever relationship the proof names. It also never checks that the resolved document's id or the method's controller is the signer, which is §4.7.3 item 2.
2. The doc comment ("as upstream does not") was not wrong when it was written. It cites VTI ed672fff, where `verify_trust_task_proof_with` called `di.verify(&unsigned, resolver, VerifyOptions::new())` with no purpose binding and there was no purpose.rs. It is stale against the VTI pin f7b78e29d, where `verify_core` binds the purpose (verify.rs:313-316, `PurposeBound::for_proof`) and `ProofPurpose::parse` refuses keyAgreement and unknown values (purpose.rs:81-94). §4.7.3 items 1-3 are MUST in both the PR branch (tt/SPEC.md:360-372) and our framework pin 2a66a0351 (SPEC.md:359-371).
3. The second part is only partly right. The PR's demo signs with proofPurpose authentication (all 14 proofs in examples/hcp-demo-ts/transcript.golden.txt, and SCENARIO.md:71). The VTA's signer picks authentication for every non-attestation slug, hcp/* included (trust_task_sign.rs:254, purpose.rs:139-150). `verifyDocumentProof`'s default (documentProof.ts:453) returns false for those documents. But the PR's own 47 spec.md examples sign hcp documents with assertionMethod, and the default would accept that shape. That itself runs against SPEC.md:374, which says a producer SHOULD sign with authentication.

Severity: note, not raise. It is a Keyring-side conformance and security gap with no ask of the PR. Interop does not break: Keyring accepts too much, and VTA replies still verify. Keyring action: bring `verifyTrustTaskProof` up to the pin's purpose binding (relationship named by proofPurpose, refuse keyAgreement and unknown values, check document id and controller). Pass an explicit purpose whenever `verifyDocumentProof` is used on hcp documents. | The core claim holds, with four narrowings. (1) Keyring's verifyTrustTaskProof (documentProof.ts:550) accepts any non-empty proofPurpose string, keyAgreement included. It looks the method up in verificationMethod plus whatever is embedded under authentication or assertionMethod (:569-572), whatever the purpose says. Its doc comment (:532-536), and the test that pins it (inboundProofs.test.ts:148, "accepts any non-empty proofPurpose, as upstream names none"), were right for the VTI commit the doc cites, ed672fff (2026-09-24). They have been out of date since a6878658a (2026-09-26, VTI-KEY-022), which is in the pin f7b78e29d. At the pin, verify_core binds the purpose (verify.rs:313-316, PurposeBound::for_proof → ProofPurpose::parse, purpose.rs:81-94, 205-209), and authorised_method requires the method under that relationship (purpose.rs:271-310). SPEC §4.7.3 items 1-3 are a MUST at our own framework pin 2a66a0351 too (SPEC.md:359-371), not only on the PR branch. (2) The practical exposure is narrower than "accepts keyAgreement". A key embedded only under keyAgreement is never found, and an X25519 key cannot make an Ed25519 signature verify. The real gap is mixing up relationships: a key listed only under authentication, or only in verificationMethod, is accepted for a proof that claims assertionMethod. (3) On the main VTA reply path, VtaClient only logs checkVtaReply's verdict and refuses nothing (VtaClient.ts:2090-2093). Today the gap affects outcomes only in foreignApproval.readReply (:141-143), ballotBoxDoor, and consentCheck. consentCheck compares the purpose string to 'authentication' separately (:93) but never checks that the key is listed under authentication. (4) The verifyDocumentProof default point is half right. A VTA-signed hcp reply would fail it: vta-service signs every response with proofPurpose authentication (trust_tasks/mod.rs:827-832). So would the PR demo's documents (transcript.golden.txt:16; SCENARIO.md:71 "proofPurpose: authentication"). But all 28 hcp spec.md examples in the PR show proofPurpose assertionMethod (for example specs/hcp/entries/create/0.1/spec.md:180). A document shaped like those passes the default's purpose check. Even then the default does not bind the relationship: it falls back to the first signing key (documentProof.ts:490-492). Severity: under this review's scale this is a Keyring-side fix with no ask of the PR, so "note" (a Keyring conformance action item), not "raise". The one thing to ask the PR about is that its spec examples use assertionMethod while the demo and SPEC §4.7.3 (producer SHOULD use authentication) do not, and no hcp proofRequirement says which purpose to use.
findings.reasons:
HOLDS: Every cited line says what the claim says, and the code is the same at Keyring origin/main. The VTA reply verifier really does skip the purpose binding that vta-sdk at the VTI pin and SPEC §4.7.3 require. Three things are overstated:
- The comment's "upstream does not" was true at the VTI commit it cites (ed672fff, which predates purpose.rs). It is stale, not a misreading.
- "Returns false on PR-signed hcp documents" is true of the demo's documents, which sign with authentication, but not of the PR's spec examples, which sign with assertionMethod.
- The finding asks nothing of the PR and does not break interop, so by the review's own scale it is a note (a Keyring-side fix), not a raise. || HOLDS: I tried to disprove the claim and could not. Keyring has no fix on origin/main or on any branch: the same doc text and the line-550 check are on origin/main c65701c91, and a pickaxe search for keyAgreement in documentProof.ts finds nothing. The vta-sdk pin binds the purpose and refuses keyAgreement and unknown values. The MUST is in SPEC §4.7.3 at our framework pin as well as on the PR branch. VTA replies are signed for authentication. What I did find narrows the claim rather than overturning it. The doc comment was accurate for the commit it cites and went out of date two days later. The keyAgreement case cannot actually be exploited with an X25519 key; the real exposure is mixing up relationships. The main VtaClient path only logs the verdict. And the PR's own hcp spec examples are signed for assertionMethod, so "PR-signed hcp documents fail the default" is true for the demo but not for the spec examples. The finding asks nothing of the PR, so "note" fits the rubric better than "raise". The PR-facing piece is the inconsistent example purposes.

findings.title: The PR's TS proof verifier only handles did:key
findings.claim: @openvtc/trust-tasks-proof's DataIntegrityProofVerifier resolves keys only from did:key (no resolver), so it cannot verify a did:webvh VTA's replies. The demo uses did:key throughout. vta-mcp is Rust and uses vta-sdk's resolver-backed verifier, so a plugin that goes through vta-mcp is unaffected.
findings.evidence: trust-tasks-ts-proof/src/verifier.ts:66-69 "did:key only — no network, no resolver"; :165-167 publicKeyFromDidKey → "verificationMethod is not a did:key this verifier supports"; README.md:70; external/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/vta-mcp/Cargo.toml name = "vta-mcp"
findings.keyringImpact: If vti-agent-connect ever talks TSP directly using the TS library, it needs a did:webvh resolver to verify the VTA.
findings.corrected: Holds as a "note", with one wording fix and two qualifiers. The did:key-only verifier is not something the PR adds. @openvtc/trust-tasks-proof (0.2.3) is the framework's existing library on main, and #1380 and #1382 change no file under trust-tasks-ts-proof/. It was already did:key-only at our pin 2a66a0351. The PR's TS demo (examples/hcp-demo-ts) uses it with did:key parties only. Its DataIntegrityProofVerifier gets the public key only from a did:key verificationMethod and refuses anything else as signatureInvalid, so it cannot verify replies from a VTA that signs as did:webvh. The library's signer is did:key-only too. The verifier is one implementation of the pluggable ProofVerifier interface (trust-tasks-ts-tsp's consumer accepts any proofVerifier), so a TS client could plug in a resolver-backed verifier instead of forking. vta-mcp is Rust and goes through vta-sdk's VtaClient (dispatch_trust_task, then verified_reply / verify_reply). That path verifies a reply through a shared DID resolver that understands did:webvh and honours PNM_RESOLVER_URL, then checks that the signer equals the VTA's DID. It skips the check only when the reply carries no proof, signed replies are not required, and the type is not load-bearing. So a plugin that goes through vta-mcp is unaffected.
findings.reasons: HOLDS: Every quote checks out on branch pr1382. verifier.ts:68-69 says "did:key only — no network, no resolver; the key travels in the identifier". At :165-167, publicKeyFromDidKey returning null leads to "verificationMethod is not a did:key this verifier supports". keys.ts:63-66 returns null unless the identifier starts with "did:key:". README.md:70 says "Keys travel in the `did:key` verification method — no resolver, no network." The demo comment at demo.ts:5 says each party has "its own did:key". The demo's package.json depends on file:../../trust-tasks-ts-proof. The Cargo.toml citation only proves the crate's name; the resolver-backed part I checked myself in the VTI source at f7b78e29d. vta-mcp/src/main.rs:50 imports vta_sdk::client::VtaClient. server.rs:900-902 calls client.dispatch_trust_task. vta-sdk/src/client/mod.rs:2188 calls verified_reply. At :2428-2445, verify_reply builds shared_did_resolver_from_env(), wraps it in TrustTaskVmResolver::from_optional and calls verify_trust_task_proof_value. :2463 checks signer != identity.vta_did. vta-sdk/Cargo.toml:112 notes that a client verifies the responses it receives. The only problem is the wording "the PR's": git diff from the merge-base to pr1380 and to pr1382 is empty for trust-tasks-ts-proof. The same did:key-only text is at our pin 2a66a0351 (verifier.ts:51, :124). That is a wording fix, not a refutation, and "note" stays the right severity.

findings.title: The transcript is not the signed bytes: accessToken is shortened before printing
findings.claim: The demo prints each document after redact(), which cuts accessToken to its first 6 characters plus an ellipsis, so the printed proofs do not verify over the printed JSON. With the full token restored, the Management Client revoke request (transcript lines 325-345) verifies, and it is quoted in full in the notes.
findings.evidence: examples/hcp-demo-ts/src/demo.ts:451-452 pretty(redact(doc)); :492-499 `${v.slice(0, 6)}…`; transcript.golden.txt:331 "accessToken": "hcp_mt…"; crosscheck.mjs control 4: false
findings.keyringImpact: Anyone using the transcript as test vectors must put the demo tokens back first (hcp_mt_demo_management; hcp_at_demo_0001 for the agent).
findings.askOfPR: Optional: say in SCENARIO.md or the README that the proofs are over the unredacted demo tokens, or print the demo tokens in full since they are demo-only.
findings.corrected: The claim holds, and "note" is the right severity. One correction to the ask: the PR already documents the redaction. SCENARIO.md:229-230 says "**Redaction:** the value of every member named `accessToken` is printed as its first 6 characters followed by `…` (U+2026)", and README.md:68 says "access tokens are redacted to their first 6 characters". The full demo tokens are already written out in SCENARIO.md's step table (:196 "`accessToken hcp_at_demo_0001`", :198 "`accessToken hcp_mt_demo_management`") and in test/demo.test.ts:26. What the PR never says outright is that each printed proofValue was computed over the unredacted document, so the printed JSON plus its proof will not verify. That matters because SCENARIO.md:72 invites cross-language byte comparison ("proofValue matches across languages"). So the optional ask comes down to one sentence beside the redaction rule in SCENARIO.md:229, or printing the demo-only tokens in full.
findings.reasons: HOLDS: I opened every citation on branch pr1382 (HEAD e163cac1d), and each says what the claim says. demo.ts:451-452 shows the print step writes `pretty(redact(doc))`. demo.ts:496 replaces any string member named accessToken with `${v.slice(0, 6)}…`. demo.ts:224-225 shows exchange() prints the document it was handed, and request() at :211-215 signs that document with signTrustTask before it returns, so the printed document carries a proof over the full token. transcript.golden.txt:331 prints "accessToken": "hcp_mt…" inside the revoke request at lines 325-345. demo.ts:111 sets MANAGEMENT_TOKEN = "hcp_mt_demo_management", and :585 passes it as the revoke's accessToken. demo.ts:366 mints `hcp_at_demo_${String(++this.tokens).padStart(4, "0")}`, which gives hcp_at_demo_0001 for the first grant, matching SCENARIO.md:196 and test/demo.test.ts:26. The Management Client's signing key is 32 bytes of 0x31 (demo.ts:162). I reran the existing crosscheck.mjs (Keyring's canonicalize + noble recipe). With the token restored, the proof verifies: true. The same proof reproduces byte-for-byte: true. Control 4, the transcript exactly as printed: false. Control 5, issuedAt rewritten to .000Z: false. notes/signing-formats.md:142-161 and :361/:381 quote the restored document and its JCS bytes in full. The only overstatement is in the ask: SCENARIO.md and the README already document the redaction and list the full tokens. What they never state is that the printed proofs do not verify over the printed JSON.

findings.title: Where JS and Rust canonical bytes could still differ
findings.claim: Key order (UTF-16 code units) and doubles (ECMAScript formatting via ryu-js) agree between the canonicalize package and serde_json_canonicalizer 0.3.2. Two differences remain. An integer above 2^53 from a Rust producer is rounded by JSON.parse in Keyring, so the proof fails there; the reverse direction is fine. A lone surrogate is accepted by JS and refused by the Rust parser. The hcp schemas declare no float members, so only open members (VC credential, audit data, narrowedTo, metadata) could carry such values.
findings.evidence: serde_json_canonicalizer-0.3.2/src/jcs.rs:27 .encode_utf16(), :205-210 ryu_js; trust-tasks-ts-proof/src/jcs.ts:12-29; grep '"number"' specs/hcp → none; _shared/0.1/context-entry.schema.json Assertion.confidence {type [string,null], enum}
findings.keyringImpact: Low. Keep in mind when Keyring verifies provider-signed documents that carry credentials or provider metadata.
findings.corrected:
Severity stays "note". Three of the claim's points are confirmed. Key order agrees: both sides sort by UTF-16 code units. Double formatting agrees: both use ECMAScript form, via ryu-js on the Rust side. A lone surrogate works only in JS: Keyring's canonicalize 1.0.8 accepts one and emits "\ud800", while serde_json 1.0.154 refuses it ("lone leading surrogate in hex escape"). So a JS-signed document with a lone surrogate cannot be checked by a Rust verifier, and no Rust producer can make such a document.

The claim about integers above 2^53 is wrong. A Rust producer's proof does NOT fail in Keyring. serde_json_canonicalizer (0.3.2 and 0.4.1 alike) writes every integer as `value as f64` and then formats it with ryu_js. So the Rust signer already signs the nearest double: 9007199254740993 becomes "9007199254740992". Keyring's JSON.parse rounds to that same double, and canonicalize prints the same digits, so the proof verifies in both directions. What actually happens is lossy binding, not a proof failure. The signature covers only the rounded double: two wire integers that round to the same double (9007199254740993 and 9007199254740992) share one valid proof, and Keyring reads the rounded value.

The claim that "only open members could carry such values" is right for floats, since no hcp schema declares "number". It is wrong for integers. Declared integer members have a minimum but no maximum: `version` (context-entry, disclosure, audit-event), `evidence` (context-entry, audit-event) and the counts in disclosures/summary. These values will never come near 2^53 in practice, though.

Version detail: the PR branch's Cargo.lock has only serde_json_canonicalizer 0.4.1, reached through affinidi-data-integrity 0.9.2, trust-tasks-ceremony and hcp-demo. 0.3.2 comes from the VTI pin's affinidi-data-integrity 0.8.0. The two versions differ only in that 0.4.1 refuses duplicate keys, which none of these points depends on. Also, the cited trust-tasks-ts-proof/src/jcs.ts is the framework's own canonicalizer. Keyring uses the npm `canonicalize` package instead (documentProof.ts:40). Both are built on JSON.stringify and Object.keys().sort(), so they behave the same here.
findings.reasons:
REFUTE: One of the claim's two "remaining differences" is false. The cited crate itself shows why. jcs.rs:133-137 (`fn write_i64 ... self.write_f64(writer, value as f64)`) and :178-182 (`fn write_u64 ... self.write_f64(writer, value as f64)`) mean a Rust producer's canonical bytes already carry the rounded double. The ryu-js tests (d2s_test.rs:51 `"1234000000000000"`) confirm integers print in ECMAScript form. A one-process node check with Keyring's canonicalize 1.0.8 on the wire `{"version":9007199254740993}` gave `{"version":9007199254740992}`, the same bytes Rust signs. So the proof verifies, and "the proof fails there" does not follow from the evidence.

The scope sentence is also overstated for integers. The hcp schemas declare integer members with no maximum, for example context-entry.schema.json:203-205 `"version": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1` and :96-98 `"evidence": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0`.

The other parts hold. Key order: jcs.rs:24-27 `.encode_utf16()` matches canonicalize.js:18 `Object.keys(object).sort()`. Double formatting: jcs.rs:209-211 `ryu_js::Buffer::new(); ... format_finite(value)`. Lone surrogate: serde_json read.rs:962-964 and :1009-1010 `ErrorCode::LoneLeadingSurrogateInHexEscape`, while node returns `{"a":"\ud800"}`. No float members: grep for '"number"' under specs/hcp finds nothing, and confidence is `"type": ["string", "null"]` at context-entry:114-116.

Unchecked: whether serde_json's float_roundtrip feature is enabled through a transitive dependency. Without it, serde_json parses floats on a best-effort basis that is not always exact, which could matter for a Rust verifier reading floats in open members. No Cargo.toml in either workspace names float_roundtrip or arbitrary_precision.

findings.title: hcp document size bounds are well above the VTA's current request caps
findings.claim: hcp/import allows a 16 MiB request, export a 14 MiB response and query a 12 MiB response. The VTA caps REST trust-task bodies at 1 MiB (hcp/* is refused over REST in V0 anyway) and agent-memory values at 64 KiB, while entries/create allows 512 KiB. I did not check TSP or DIDComm carriage limits for documents this large.
findings.evidence: specs/hcp/import/0.1/spec.md:57 request: 16777216; export/0.1/spec.md:58 response: 14680064; entries/query/0.1/spec.md:57 response: 12582912; vta-service/src/routes/mod.rs:82-84 MAX_BODY_SIZE = 1024 * 1024; vta-service/src/operations/app_state.rs:94 MAX_VALUE_BYTES = 65_536; vti2823 hcp.md:161 REST refused
findings.keyringImpact: Export and import through Keyring would need a carriage that can move multi-MiB documents, and Keyring holding them in memory. Not in the V0 demo.
findings.corrected: Severity stays "note". Every cited number is correct, but two of the comparisons need narrowing. The PR declares these bounds: hcp/import request 16777216 (16 MiB), hcp/export response 14680064 (14 MiB), hcp/entries/query response 12582912 (12 MiB), and hcp/entries/create request 524288 (512 KiB). They are the same on pr1380 and pr1382. (1) The VTA's MAX_BODY_SIZE = 1024 * 1024 is a request-body limit (DefaultBodyLimit) on its HTTP routes, `/trust-tasks` included. Of these bounds, only import's 16 MiB request is over it. The 14 MiB export and 12 MiB query bounds are response sizes, and this limit does not apply to them. (2) The 64 KiB MAX_VALUE_BYTES limit covers agent memory (`vta/memory/*`), not HCP entries. VTI's design keeps entries in their own `hcp_entries` keyspace, and our HCP companion says `vta/memory/*` does not change. So entries/create's 512 KiB is not in conflict with it. (3) "hcp/* refused over REST in V0" is from the PR #2823 design. The pinned VTA (f7b78e29d) has no hcp code at all. (4) The PR already provides a fallback: an import over the bound is refused `malformedRequest`, and an export over it is refused `hcp:exportTooLarge` (never truncated). In both cases the PR's answer is HCP's HTTP binding. TSP and DIDComm limits on carrying documents this large remain unchecked.
findings.reasons: HOLDS: I opened every citation. The spec bounds are on the lines given (import:57, export:58, query:57; create:53 is 524288), and they match on both PR branches. routes/mod.rs:84 is MAX_BODY_SIZE = 1024 * 1024, applied globally at :478 via DefaultBodyLimit::max. The `/trust-tasks` POST route sits under it (:340-355). app_state.rs:94 is MAX_VALUE_BYTES = 65_536, and memory.rs:1-20 confirms it is the limit for the `vta/memory/*` store. hcp.md:161 says "`hcp/*` refused: REST carries no sender binding". So the claim holds and is correctly hedged on TSP and DIDComm. It is overstated in two places. First, it groups response bounds (export, query) with a request-body limit. Second, it sets the agent-memory value limit against entries/create, but hcp.md:530 puts HCP entries in their own `hcp_entries` keyspace. The pinned VTA has no hcp code, so the REST refusal is design, not current behavior. The import and export specs also name HCP's HTTP binding as the route for larger documents.

findings.title: HCP's VC Evidence profile does not list eddsa-jcs-2022 for content credentials
findings.claim: HCP 14.5 says a content credential MUST be secured with eddsa-rdfc-2022 (must verify), ecdsa-sd-2023 (should) or VC-JOSE-COSE (may), and a provider rejects other mechanisms as credential-invalid. Keyring's VRC v3 uses eddsa-rdfc-2022, which fits. The shared-connect credential uses eddsa-jcs-2022, which would be refused as an entry's content.
findings.evidence: hcp-spec/spec/2.0-draft-3/specification.md:3113-3121 table and "An implementation MUST verify eddsa-rdfc-2022"; :3129-3131 14.6 "secured with a mechanism the HCP Provider does not verify"; Keyring packages/core/src/modules/vrc/vrc-manager.ts:499-539 EDDSA_RDFC_2022; trust-tasks/module/sharedConnectCredential.ts:20 const JCS = 'eddsa-jcs-2022'
findings.keyringImpact: If Keyring writes credentials as HCP entries (the VC Evidence profile, H3 in the VTI plan), use the rdfc-secured VRC form.
findings.corrected: Holds, severity note. HCP 14.5 (spec.md:3114, "A credential that is an entry's content MUST be secured by one of the following") lists only eddsa-rdfc-2022 (verify MUST), ecdsa-sd-2023 (SHOULD) and vc-jose-cose (MAY). The discovery schema backs this up: in schemas/2.0-draft-3/discovery.json:226-245, vc_securing.issues and .verifies are each an enum of those three values, so a provider has no way to declare eddsa-jcs-2022. Under 14.5:3124 and 14.6:3133, a content credential secured any other way is rejected as credential-invalid. A jcs credential attached with role `supports` is different: 14.8 keeps it and marks it failed, and the entry is accepted. Keyring's shared-connect VRC defaults to eddsa-jcs-2022 (sharedConnectDecisions.ts:39), so it would be refused as an entry's content. Keyring's VC 2.0 VRC uses eddsa-rdfc-2022 only for RCE v3+ peers (vrc-manager.ts:526-541); older peers get Ed25519Signature2018, which is also outside the table. The rdfc form matches only on the securing mechanism. It still has to meet 14.2: a provider must canonicalize it with Keyring's own contexts (DTG or hardware-evidence), which is why the VTI plan's H3 row says "pinned contexts". Its credentialSubject.id must be the entry's subject.id, and 14.6 requires the provider to resolve a DID issuer. Whether a VRC meets these is UNVERIFIED. Line fix: the 14.6 bullet is at :3133, not :3129-3131.
